```js
async function requireSecrets() {
  // attempts getSecret() for every REQUIRED_SECRET_NAMES entry
  // throws listing ALL missing names at once (not just the first)
}
```

# Secrets Management

## Overview

This app resolves all secrets through `secrets.js`. No secret value is
ever hard-coded or placed directly in `process.env`.

```
.env.test  ──► secrets.js  ──►  AWS Secrets Manager  (production)
                           └──►  .env.test values     (development)
```

## How it works

| Layer | File | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Secret discovery | `.env.test` | Defines the **names** (keys) of every required secret. Values are used only as a local development fallback. |
| Secret resolution | `secrets.js` | Exports `getSecret(name)` and `loadAllSecrets()`. Routes all secret access through one place. |
| Application | `app.js` | Calls `loadAllSecrets()` at startup, then uses `getSecret(name)` inside routes as needed. |

## Environment modes

### Development (`NODE_ENV=development`)

`getSecret(name)` reads the value from `.env.test` — no AWS credentials or
network access required.

```bash
NODE_ENV=development node app.js
```

### Production / Staging (any other `NODE_ENV`)

`getSecret(name)` fetches the secret from **AWS Secrets Manager** using the
`@aws-sdk/client-secrets-manager` SDK. Results are cached in-process for the
lifetime of the Node process.

Required environment variables for AWS access:

| Variable | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `AWS_REGION` | Secrets Manager region (defaults to `us-east-1`) |
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | AWS credential (or use an IAM role / instance profile) |
| `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | AWS credential (or use an IAM role / instance profile) |

> **Tip:** On EC2 / ECS / Lambda, attach an IAM role instead of providing
> static key variables.

## Required secrets

The canonical list of required secrets is derived from `.env.test` at
startup and printed to stdout:

```
[secrets] Required secrets: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ...
```

To add or remove a secret, update `.env.test` — the application discovers
the list automatically.

## AWS Secrets Manager setup

Create one secret per key, e.g.:

```bash
aws secretsmanager create-secret \
  --name DATABASE_URL \
  --secret-string "postgres://user:password@host:5432/db"
```

The secret name in Secrets Manager **must match** the key name in `.env.test`.

Alternatively, store all secrets as a single JSON object and parse individual
fields from the returned object inside `getSecret`.

## Minimum IAM policy

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": "secretsmanager:GetSecretValue",
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:secretsmanager:<REGION>:<ACCOUNT_ID>:secret:DATABASE_URL-*",
        "arn:aws:secretsmanager:<REGION>:<ACCOUNT_ID>:secret:STRIPE_SECRET_KEY-*"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/health` | Liveness check |
| GET | `/users` | Example data endpoint |
| GET | `/db-status` | Resolves `DATABASE_URL` and returns connection metadata (no credentials exposed) |
| GET | `/config-check` | Verifies all required secrets resolve; returns names + status, never values |

| `USE_LOCAL_SECRETS=true` | Same as above — useful for CI or integration tests without AWS |
| `AWS_REGION` / `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` | Tells the SDK which region to use |
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` + `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | Standard SDK credential chain (not required when running on EC2/ECS/Lambda with an IAM role) |
| `PORT` | Overrides the default listen port of `3000` |
